text: Head: eye inflammation/unusual redness suggests respiratory disease; eyelids stuck together are seen in Coryza; heavy watery eye discharge is seen in Avian Influenza and Infectious Bronchitis; Marek's disease causes tumors leading to irregularly shaped pupils and blindness. Mouth: pus or mucus suggests respiratory disease (Coryza, Mycoplasma, Fowl Cholera, Infectious Bronchitis); membranes and ulcers are seen in the wet form of Fowl Pox. Neck/trachea: clear exudate in the cut trachea suggests Infectious Bronchitis; bloody mucus suggests Avian Influenza, Laryngo-tracheitis, or Newcastle Disease; red worms are commonly found in scavenging chickens. Muscle: after removing the skin from neck to cloaca, emaciated muscle suggests chronic disease or poor nutrition; bruising (hemorrhage) can come from trauma or from Staphylococcus infection, and hemorrhages on the thighs specifically suggest Gumboro disease.
